title: Patient-Level Expression Programs in Human Breast Cancer: NMF Decomposition and Stability Assessment
content: Breast cancer differs substantially between patients in molecular and cellular properties. This variation is captured at a cellular resolution by single-cell RNA sequencing. However, comparing patterns of ligand-receptor expression across patients remains challenging, particularly when differences in cellular composition contribute to the observed variation. In this study, I analysed a comprehensive breast cancer single-cell atlas that contained data from 138 patients and over 620,000 cells across 8 studies. Then, I constructed patient-level features for each receptor-ligand pair by taking a weighted mean of their expression product across cell types. The weight of each cell type was determined by its abundance and zero-variance features were removed after scaling the matrix obtained from processing. I then used non-negative matrix factorisation (NMF) on the patients’ data and checked the stability of the components from ranks five to twelve and ten random initializations for each rank. This was followed by an investigation of the association of NMF-generated program scores with annotated disease categories. The resulting matrix had 3,465 features. The ten-component model had a relative reconstruction error of 0.5862. The stability of the components changed with ranks. For instance, the mean matched cosine similarity was highest at rank seven (0.9446), while rank ten offered lower reconstruction error. Seven non-overlapping programs were associated across disease categories before adjustment for study and six retained associations after adjustment. Subsequently, I performed a comparison of estrogen receptor-positive and triple-negative patients within the study. Five programs showed significant difference. Overall, the study uncovers consistent patterns in patient-level, abundance-weighted ligand-receptor expression characteristics. The decomposition captures variation across patients and disease types that will need to be further studied for its biological interpretation along with functional and clinical evidence.
